root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Richter Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. d4 g6

overview: Black recaptures on d5 with the knight, or plays ...g6 first, preparing ...Bg7 and ...Nxd5 with a hypermodern set-up against White's centre. White gains space with Nf3, c4 and Be2 and develops easily, while Black develops with ...Bg7, ...O-O and ...Nb6 to hit the centre. The position is Caro-Kann-like in solidity but with a fianchettoed bishop.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nf3, Be2 and O-O and gain space with c4
Kick the d5 knight with c4 and c3 pawn structures
Use the space and pieces to aim for a slight edge

black_ideas.idea: Castle short and break with ...c5 or ...e5 at the right moment
Play for a compact set-up and counter-strike on the centre

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on c4, d4 vs Black ...Nb6/...Bg7
Semi-open structure with an open d-file

character.notes: Solid enough for Black with a fianchetto, and White has an easy space edge; not forcing.

gambit.notes: The pawn is regained at once with ...Nxd5.

structure.notes: Scandinavian semi-open structure with Black pieces hitting the centre.

approach.notes: The Modern Scandinavian is played by strong players, so standard.

sublines_that_differ.name: Icelandic Gambit (3.c4 e6)
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. c4 e6
sublines_that_differ.how: A different branch: Black offers a pawn for development.

character.reason: Black fianchetto against White space; neither forcing nor impregnable.

gambit.reason: The pawn is regained at once.

structure.reason: Scandinavian structure with the d-file open.

plans.reason: Black sets a bishop on g7 and hits the centre with the knight.
